newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MURRIN MURRIN SALE BOOSTS ANACONDA PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: MURRIN MURRIN SALE BOOSTS ANACONDA PROFIT.

text.p: Nickel project developer Anaconda Nickel Ltd said on Tuesday that its net profit for the year ended June 30 was A$54.35 million.
This included an abnormal profit of A$57.86 million booked on the sale of 40 percent of its Murrin Murrin nickel project in Western Australia to Swiss resources house Glencore International Ag.
The company reported a net loss of A$1.28 million in the year to June 1996. The 1996/97 operating loss before abnormal items and tax was A$3.51 million.
Earlier, Anaconda said it had executed definitive agreements regarding the sale of the 40 percent stake to Glencore following the announcement of the sale in November 1996.

The changes to the original binding letter of intent follow the securing of project finance by way of a A$110 million debt facility through Natwest Capital Markets and a A$96.4 million placement of shares to institutional investors.
The A$900 million project is scheduled to come on stream at the end of 1998 and to reach production of 45,000 tonnes of nickel and 3,000 tonnes of cobalt in that year.
Glencore, which also has a 19 percent stake in Anaconda, has exclusive rights to sell the cobalt and nickel.

Anaconda has plans to expand annual production to 75,000 tonnes of nickel and 5,000 tonnes of cobalt once the base plant is commissioned. By 3.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), Anaconda shares were seven cents lower at A$3.60 in thin trade of A$3.60.
